metrics.description: Fraction of evaluator-generated stimulus sequences (shipped + hidden random + adversarial) for which recovered_fsm's out waveform exactly matches the reference flattened_netlist.v simulation, cycle by cycle, via iverilog/vvp simulation.
metrics.name: functional_equivalence

metrics.description: Whether the submission expresses the FSM using word-level behavioral RTL (state register(s), always block, case/if-based transition logic) rather than gate-primitive instantiation, checked via banned-construct static scan of primitives.v module names inside recovered_rtl.v.
metrics.name: word_recovery_rate

metrics.description: Interface conformance score: correctness of module name 'recovered_fsm' and exact port list (clk, rst, in, out with correct directions/widths) as required for the evaluator's testbench to instantiate the submission.

metrics.description: Whether iverilog successfully compiles submission/recovered_rtl.v together with the generated testbench with zero errors.

acceptance_criteria: iverilog compiles submission/recovered_rtl.v plus an evaluator-authored testbench without errors.
For the shipped stimulus.txt sequence, recovered_fsm's out sequence matches the reference netlist's out sequence on every cycle.
For >=5 hidden pseudo-random sequences (length >=64) and >=2 adversarial sequences designed around the '1011' boundary cases, recovered_fsm's out matches the reference netlist's out on every cycle.
Static banned-construct scan finds no direct instantiation of primitives.v gate modules and no textual copy of flattened_netlist.v content inside recovered_rtl.v.
recovered_fsm module has exactly ports clk, rst, in, out with correct 1-bit directions.
hidden_spec.ground_truth: The flattened netlist implements a 4-state Moore FSM that detects the non-overlapping serial pattern '1011' on input 'in', asserting 'out'=1 for exactly one clock cycle when the pattern completes, then returning to the initial state to search again. Internally the netlist uses two flip-flops (state encoded as S0=00, S1=01, S2=10, S3=11 in the gate netlist, but the encoding is obscured by XOR-mixed gate logic and non-mnemonic net names) plus combinational next-state and output logic built from NAND/NOR/XOR primitives instantiated from primitives.v. A correct recovery need not use the same encoding, only equivalent behavior.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Static banned-construct scan (fail-on-presence only) of submission/recovered_rtl.v for instantiations of primitive module names defined in inputs/primitives.v (e.g. NAND2, NOR2, XOR2, DFF) or direct textual inclusion of inputs/flattened_netlist.v; presence causes FAIL regardless of simulated correctness.
security_requirements.requirement: The recovered RTL must not merely re-embed the original gate-level netlist verbatim (e.g. by wrapping primitives.v gates inside recovered_fsm); it must be expressed at the word/register level using synthesizable behavioral constructs, so that the recovery step reflects genuine structural understanding rather than pass-through obfuscation.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Interface conformance check: recovered_fsm must have exactly the four ports clk, rst, in, out with correct directions and 1-bit widths; extra ports cause FAIL.
security_requirements.requirement: The recovered module must not leak or depend on any internal debug/backdoor signal that might exist in the flattened netlist beyond the public clk/rst/in/out interface.

security_requirements.detection_strategy: Evaluator generates hidden randomized and adversarial stimulus sequences at grading time (not shipped in inputs/) and compares cycle-by-cycle output against the reference netlist simulation.
security_requirements.requirement: Behavioral equivalence must hold under adversarial/edge-case input sequences (e.g. repeated resets mid-pattern, back-to-back overlapping near-matches like '10110111011'), not just the sample stimulus, to rule out a submission that overfits to the shipped stimulus file.

hidden_spec.threat_model: A flattened, gate-level netlist with meaningless net names (e.g. n12, n47) and gate-mixed state encoding obscures the control intent of the design, preventing engineers from auditing, verifying, or safely modifying the controller logic. This mirrors reverse-engineering-resistant obfuscation used to hide IP or malicious backdoors in third-party sequential IP cores.

constraints: Do not modify any file under inputs/; submit only submission/recovered_rtl.v.
The submitted file must be self-contained (single module, no external includes).

Do not instantiate or reference any gate-level primitive modules from primitives.v; the recovered design must be written at the word/register level (using synthesizable Verilog operators and always blocks), not a copy of the flattened gate netlist.
The module must use a single clock domain and a synchronous active-high reset as described in design_brief.md.
expected_outputs: submission/recovered_rtl.v containing a single Verilog module named 'recovered_fsm' with the pinned port list
The recovered module must produce, cycle-for-cycle, the same 'out' sequence as the original netlist for the provided stimulus and for additional hidden stimulus sequences

functional_requirements.requirement: recovered_rtl.v must define a module named exactly 'recovered_fsm' with ports: input clk, input rst, input in, output out (all 1-bit, 'out' driven combinationally or registered such that it updates on the clk edge consistent with a Moore machine).
When rst is asserted for one clock cycle and then held low, the module must reproduce the exact reset-then-run output sequence recorded in stimulus.txt for the given 'in' sequence.
The module must compile cleanly with iverilog (no undeclared identifiers, no unresolved module references) as a standalone file requiring no other source files.

For at least 5 distinct pseudo-random input sequences of length >= 64 cycles applied after reset, the recovered module's 'out' waveform must match the reference netlist's 'out' waveform on every cycle.

public_spec.interface: File: submission/recovered_rtl.v. It must define exactly one top-level module: `module recovered_fsm(input clk, input rst, input in, output out);`. Signal meanings: clk = free-running clock (evaluation drives it), rst = synchronous active-high reset (when asserted for one or more rising edges, the FSM must return to its initial/reset state on the next rising edge and hold that state's output), in = single-bit control input sampled on each rising edge of clk, out = single-bit Moore output that reflects the current state (may be combinational function of internal state registers, but must be stable between clock edges and change only in response to clk edges). Evaluation instantiates this exact module name/port list in a generated testbench alongside the reference netlist (via inputs/flattened_netlist.v + inputs/primitives.v) and compares 'out' cycle by cycle.
public_spec.objective: You are given a flattened gate-level netlist of a small synchronous sequential circuit implemented with basic gates and D flip-flops. The netlist implements a Moore-style finite state machine with one input bit, one output bit, a clock, and an active-high synchronous reset. Your task is to analyze the netlist and produce a clean, human-readable word-level Verilog module that behaves identically to the original circuit for all input sequences: same output on every clock cycle, given the same input and reset sequence.
public_spec.response_format: A single Verilog source file at submission/recovered_rtl.v containing the module 'recovered_fsm' as specified in the interface. No other files are graded.

title: Recover an FSM from a Flattened Sequential Netlist
